_about: Starter rubric for tools/rubric-marker.html. Edit the text and numbers, keep the shape. Keys starting with _ are notes and are ignored. Required: format, id, title, bands, parts, strands, criteria. Each strand needs a band descriptor (bands[].d), a 'can' phrase and a 'next' phrase for every band up to its maxBand (1-4), plus 'start' (the next step for band 0). Each criterion is one question or part-question: its marks (max), which strand it is evidence for, and which band of that strand. Every band of every strand needs at least one criterion. A criterion counts towards its band at half its marks or more (change with 'pass'). Leave a strand's weight out and it is the sum of its criteria's marks. Optional: code (a curriculum code shown beside the strand), sub (a short label; defaults to the question numbers), noun (what the task and its items are called in comments), columnOrder ('listed' or 'question'), context, eyebrow, subtitle, theme, fileStem, total (checked against the sum of the marks).
title: Practical Investigation Report

strands.name: Plans a fair test
strands.start: name the one thing being changed in the experiment

bands.d: States an aim for the investigation.
Identifies the independent and dependent variables.
Lists the variables to control and how each is kept the same.
Writes a testable hypothesis with a reason drawn from science ideas.

can: state an aim for an investigation
pick out the variable changed and the variable measured
say which variables must be controlled, and how
write a hypothesis that can be tested and give a scientific reason for it
next: name the variable changed and the variable measured in each investigation
list everything else that could affect the result, then say how {their} method keeps each the same
add a reason to the hypothesis using the science behind the experiment
plan a follow-up experiment that would test the hypothesis further

strands.name: Processes and represents data
strands.start: record each measurement in a table with a heading and a unit

bands.d: Records results in a table with headings and units.
Calculates an average for repeated trials.
Draws a graph of the right type with labelled axes and units.
Identifies a pattern in the data and any result that does not fit it.

can: record results clearly in a table with units
calculate the average of repeated trials
choose and draw the right kind of graph, with labelled axes
describe the pattern in a set of data and spot a result that does not fit
next: practise averaging repeated trials, leaving out any result that is clearly wrong
decide between a line graph and a bar graph by asking whether the variable changed is a number
describe the pattern in words using both variables, in the form “as one increases, the other increases or decreases”
explain what might have caused a result that does not fit the pattern

strands.name: Draws conclusions and evaluates the method
strands.start: say whether the results supported the hypothesis

bands.d: States whether the results support the hypothesis.
Uses data from the results to justify the conclusion.
Suggests an improvement to the method and explains how it would help.

can: say whether the results supported the hypothesis
back up a conclusion with figures from the results
suggest an improvement to the method and explain why it would make the results more reliable
next: quote at least one figure from the results when writing the conclusion
look for one weakness in the method and suggest a specific fix
connect the improvement to reliability or accuracy, and say which
